Dear Mr. Farmani,

Polygon is delighted to consider partnering with you to roll out Holly's clothing line into the South American market.

The accompanying proposal was drawn up in response to the suggestions discussed with you by Miranda Morehouse and to your concerns and priorities. Here is an overview of the proposal content we want to move ahead with:

Holly's Opportunity/Challenge
  • Strategic timing: Staggering rise of sales in S.A. clothing market (e.g., Brazil, Colombia)
  • Few North American lines have entered the market
  • Holly's need for PR and publicity in S.A. market

Polygon's Strategy/Contribution
  • Polygon's leading market record and established reputation allows us to be fully prepared to move along with global expansion
  • Polygon's informed preparation to enter into the market – Test Everything: Assume Nothing approach
  • Polygon's innovative approach to new marketing trends includes innovative media plans
    • Staff with culturally relevant PR experience (i.e., Fernando Rosado)
    • Familiarity with keeping up with global media trends like social media, blogs, platforms, and Internet articles
    • Financially prudent strategy: high Pl media, platforms and other online channels

Polygon is a personalized business that bases its strategy on the client's business objectives, PR goals and budget. Our proven track record of success in North America, combined with awareness of rapidly changing media forums and the complexities of marketing cross-culturally would make us an invaluable partner. Thank you for this opportunity to consider what we believe could turn into to an extremely successful alliance.

Sincerely,
Peter Smith
(for Janet Ellison)

A phrasal verb is a verb and a preposition that have a different meaning together than they do on their own.
  • Some phrasal verbs have to stay together. They are called inseparable phrasal verbs.
  • Some phrasal verbs can be separated. They are called separable phrasal verbs.
  • Some phrasal verbs have three parts.
Separable phrasal verbs always require an object.

Examples:
We will roll out the clothing line slowly.
We will roll the clothing line out slowly.
If the object of the sentence is a pronoun, it must go between the two parts of the phrasal verb.

Example:
We will roll it out slowly.

Some phrasal verbs are inseparable, so the verb must be directly followed by its preposition. Otherwise, the meaning of the phrasal verb will be incorrect. Three word phrasal verbs are always inseparable.

Examples:
It is important to keep up with all fashion trends.
They are prepared to enter into the market.

In the business world, proposals are vital when you want to make a sales deal. Writing a good proposal can help you achieve your goals. Remember that a proposal is your selling tool. A well-written proposal will show that you have thoroughly understood what your client needs and you have a good solution.
In order to write a good proposal, you need to make sure you include the following:

1. An Opening Statement: thank your client for the opportunity to present your proposal
    (company x) is delighted to consider partnering with you to + (verb) ...

  2. A Scope of Work Statement: write a short description showing your understanding of the client's needs and the solutions you are proposing to address them
    This proposal responds to the suggestions discussed ...

  3. Matching the company to the requirements and situation: describe how your company matches the client's requirements and their situation
    We are a leader in the market and are prepared for ...
    Our team / staff are experienced in ...
    Our company bases its strategy on the client's objectives, requirements and budget.
    Our success in the North American / Asian market makes us an invaluable / high powered partner.

  4. Thank-you statement: thank the client for the opportunity
    Thank you for the chance / opportunity to build / create a successful alliance.
Example: The accompanying proposal was drawn up in response to the suggestions discussed with you by Miranda Morehouse.
These are words you use when writing a business proposal.
Example: The staggering rise of sales in the South American clothing market is what we wanted to see.
good knowledge of a specific subject
Example: Their familiarity with keeping up with global media trends is impressive.
the type of computer system or software that someone used
Example: Polygon keeps up with all platforms.
a system that you use to send or obtain information
Example: We intend to use all other online channels.
details that make it hard to understand or deal with something
Example: We are able to deal with the complexities of marketing cross-culturally.
Example: Our proven track-record of success makes us an invaluable partner.
two or more companies working together to achieve something
Example: We believe this could turn into a successful alliance between the two companies.
Brainstorm ideas (on a piece of paper) of what you want to say to the business you are appealing to.
With those ideas in mind, start outlining the overall organization of your business proposal.
Introduce the company and state your purpose for writing the proposal.
Outline the client's/business' situation and describe how your company is suited to match and meet the client's/business' situation.
End your proposal by thanking the client.
